title: SRE Weekly Update - 2026-06-06
content:
Summary:
- Quiet week overall but two customer-facing incidents required on-call escalation.
- SLO status: error budget consumption increased for hosted-api write path; follow-up mitigation work scheduled.
- On-call handoff notes and playbook updates at bottom.

Incidents (high level):
1) Incident INC-SRE-2026-06-03-A (Customer-facing latency spike)
   - Window: 2026-06-03 02:10 UTC -- 2026-06-03 02:48 UTC
   - Impact: elevated p95/p99 latency for the hosted text-generation endpoint (hosted-api-v2). Several customer requests hit > 3s latency; few timed out at 10s.
   - Root cause (investigation summary): gradual increase in backend KV cache eviction due to a config regression in the cache-sizing change rolled on 2026-06-01 (PR infra#792). Under a specific request mix, cache miss amplification caused excessive compute load on the serve fleet and backpressure to async queues.
   - Mitigation: rolled back the cache-sizing change at 02:30 UTC (config revert), scaled up dedicated serving pool by +15% and increased autoscaler aggressiveness for 30 minutes. Latency recovered to baseline by 02:48 UTC.
   - Customer communication: Status page updated, two support escalations handled by CS with templated note.
   - Follow-ups / action items: see JIRA SRE-421 (assigned to Priya, due 2026-06-13) for permanent fix + improved load tests.

2) Incident INC-SRE-2026-06-05-B (Orchestration job backlog causing routing timeouts)
   - Window: 2026-06-05 14:05 UTC -- 2026-06-05 14:40 UTC
   - Impact: internal control-plane requests (rollout coordination) delayed; not directly customer-facing but caused a small increase in failed canary rollouts.
   - Root cause: a spike in CI-triggered cleanup jobs congested the orchestration queue; backpressure because queue consumers hit a transient resource starvation on a subset of nodes.
   - Mitigation: paused non-critical cleanup jobs, restarted the affected consumer service, tuned queue worker concurrency.
   - Follow-ups: add priority queueing and circuit-breaker logic (JIRA SRE-418, owner Diego, due 2026-06-20).

SLOs and Metrics (past 7 days):
- Hosted API availability (prod): 99.96% (target 99.95%) — still within SLO but error budget consumption accelerated due to small blips.
- Generation p95 latency (prod): 420ms (baseline ~380ms); p99 at 1.6s (baseline ~1.2s) — spike during 06-03 incident drove p99 up.
- Error budget remaining for hosted-api: ~73% for the current 30d window; write-path submetric saw ~18% of week’s budget used.
- On-call MTTA/MTTR: MTTA median 4m, MTTR median 28m (improved from prior week MTTR 35m).

Operational notes / runbook updates:
- Runbook: cache-sizing-and-eviction (Confluence) updated with an additional checklist for rollback and automated alert thresholds; added a quick rollback script (infra repo).
- Added a new monitoring alert: threshold for cache-miss amplification (alerts when miss-rate * eviction-rate exceeds threshold) — alert is experimental and routed to #sre-urgent.
- Orchestration queues: temporary mitigation implemented; long-term change requires priority queueing and improved backpressure signals.

On-call handoffs and coverage:
- Current rotation: Week of 2026-06-01 to 2026-06-07 -> Primary: Priya Shah; Secondary: Diego Ramos; Shadow: Jordan Park
- Handoff notes from Priya (06-06): watch for residual impact of cache rollback; verify canaries for infra#792 once the fix branch is merged. Priya to check SLO dashboards at start-of-day.
- Next rotation (starting 2026-06-08): Primary: Diego Ramos; Secondary: Aisha Malik

Action items and owners (short list):
- SRE-421 (Priya): permanent fix for cache-sizing logic + add load tests to reproduce miss amplification; due 2026-06-13.
- SRE-418 (Diego): add priority queueing + circuit-breaker to orchestration queue; due 2026-06-20.
- Infra-794 (Jordan): add automated rollback runbook script to infra repo and unit test it; due 2026-06-10.
- Observability-233 (Aisha): refine alert thresholds and add dashboard panel for cache miss amplification; due 2026-06-09.

Upcoming work / schedule:
- 2026-06-08: All-hands runbook review session (30m) to walk through cache eviction rollback steps and new alert behavior. Invite list: eng-sre, serving-runtime, infra.
- 2026-06-10: Canary for cache-size permanent fix (SRE-421) targeted; small cohort with enhanced tracing enabled.
- 2026-06-15: Postmortem review for INC-SRE-2026-06-03-A with product and serving-runtime teams.

Notes / misc:
- A reminder to keep customer-facing templates up-to-date (PR to CS templates in progress).
- We should prioritize making the cache sizing change gated behind a feature-flag in the future to avoid broad rollout regressions.

Meeting notes (weekly SRE sync 2026-06-05):
- Action review: most items on last week’s list completed; infra work for orchestration was in-progress and prioritized.
- Incident review: quick overview of timeline for 06-03; agreed that alerting thresholds were too coarse and that we need a small synthetic test exercising cache behavior.
- Capacity: discussed planned Dedicated fleet scale-up for mid-June to support enterprise customer X; SRE to prepare scaling playbook and warm-up procedures.

Appendix: quick links and artifacts
- Incident timelines and timelines export: JIRA INC-SRE-2026-06-03-A (internal)
- Runbook links: Confluence /display/SRE/Runbooks#cache-sizing-and-eviction
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/792 (cache change rolled 2026-06-01)
- Slack incident thread: #sre-ops link (see linked artifacts above)

If you have anything to add before this goes final, drop edits inline or ping on Slack.
summary_lines: Two incidents this week; main customer-facing latency spike caused by cache-sizing regression; rollback + scaling mitigated.
SLOs remain within target but error budget consumption increased for hosted-api write path.
Follow-up tickets created: SRE-421 (cache fix), SRE-418 (queue priority and circuit-breakers).
